title: an orphan running node with no process is adopted, not re-implemented
proves: a node left status running with an invocation whose provider process is no longer alive, but whose stdout log already holds a complete done envelope, is recovered by recoverOrphan reading that persisted stream and adopting it (kind: adopted) rather than restarting the worker: the run finishes without ever dispatching a second invocation. This mirrors test/helpers.mjs's own recipe for the same scenario (used by the unit test 'resume adopts an orphaned worker result instead of repeating the work'): let a node complete for real, once, so its invocation's stdout log is a real finished replay-bin.mjs transcript, then rewind the node's own status back to running (as if the controller had died before it ever processed that already-finished invocation) and recreate the attempt worktree the earlier full completion had already sealed and removed, since the recovered result still has to be re-verified and re-sealed against a real workspace.

contract.goal: prove an orphaned running node with a finished stream is adopted, not re-dispatched
